title: Stack Journey
description: Stack design, expression parsing, recursion, monotonic boundaries, and greedy simulations.

prerequisites: Basic recursion before the recursive manipulation milestone
journey.outcome: Recognize pending-work stacks, parse nested expressions, and turn monotonic boundaries into spans, areas, and greedy decisions.

connections.implement-stack-using-array: Start with the contract: the last item pushed is the first item popped. Later problems will change what the stack stores, but not this rule.
connections.reverse-a-string-using-stack: Use your stack to reverse arrival order. This makes LIFO concrete before the next problem asks you to match nested pairs.
connections.valid-parentheses: Instead of reversing everything, remove only the latest unmatched opening bracket. The stack now represents unfinished work, not just stored values.
connections.min-stack: Attach useful information to each stack state: the minimum so far. This prepares you to ask what information a future query actually needs to retain.
connections.validate-stack-sequences: Use the same push/pop contract to simulate a proposed output order. The stack now certifies whether a sequence is achievable, rather than computing a minimum.
connections.evaluate-reverse-polish-notation: Replace unfinished brackets with unfinished arithmetic. A postfix operator consumes the two most recent operands, so operand order matters for subtraction and division.
connections.infix-to-postfix-conversion: Now produce the notation you just evaluated. Keep pending operators on a stack, resolving them by precedence, parentheses, and associativity rather than arrival order alone.
connections.basic-calculator-ii: Combine tokenization with the precedence rules from infix conversion. Finish multiplication and division before adding signed terms; multi-digit numbers require a parsing state.
connections.decode-string: Move from arithmetic precedence to nested contexts. Each opening bracket saves an outer prefix and repeat count; each closing bracket completes exactly one suspended frame.
connections.simplify-path: Use the nested-context idea without recursion. A parent-directory token cancels the most recent real directory, while repeated separators and current-directory tokens add no work.
connections.insert-at-bottom-of-stack: Begin explicit recursion by removing the top until the stack is empty, placing one value, then restoring saved values during unwinding. The call stack holds temporary state.
connections.reverse-a-stack: Reuse insertion at the bottom as a subroutine. Reverse the smaller stack recursively, then place the removed top underneath it; account for the nested linear work.
connections.sort-a-stack: Change only the reinsertion rule from recursive reversal. Insert a saved value into its sorted position while preserving the already sorted remainder of the stack.
connections.nearest-greater-to-left: Nearest Greater to Left (NGL) introduces a monotonic stack. Unlike Min Stack, discard smaller or equal candidates: the current value is closer and at least as useful to future queries.
connections.next-greater-element: Nearest Greater to Right (NGR) changes only the scan direction. Keep the same strict-greater comparison and traverse from right to left.
connections.nearest-smaller-to-left: Nearest Smaller to Left (NSL) returns to a left-to-right scan and reverses the comparison. You now have independent choices for direction and stack ordering.
connections.next-smaller-element: Nearest Smaller to Right (NSR) completes the four combinations. Together, NSL and NSR will locate both ends of a histogram rectangle.
connections.stock-span: Reuse NGL, but store indices instead of values. The distance to the previous strictly higher price counts consecutive days with prices no greater than today's.
connections.largest-rectangle-in-histogram: Maximum Area Histogram (MAH) combines NSL and NSR indices. Each bar supplies a height; its two smaller boundaries supply the widest legal rectangle.
connections.trapping-rain-water: Reuse the histogram's boundary reasoning, but measure empty space instead of solid bars. A decreasing stack closes a valley when a taller right wall arrives; do not reuse the histogram area formula unchanged.
connections.maximal-rectangle: Return to MAH and lift it into two dimensions. Consecutive ones in each column form a histogram for each matrix row, so your existing area solver becomes a subroutine.
connections.next-greater-element-ii: Return to NGR and allow wraparound. A virtual second traversal exposes circular neighbors without changing the monotonic-stack invariant.
connections.daily-temperatures: Return to a linear NGR scan, but report how far away the answer is. Retain unresolved indices, not just temperatures, so a warmer day can complete many waiting answers.
connections.sum-of-subarray-minimums: Generalize NSL and NSR from finding one rectangle to counting all subarrays owned by a minimum. Equal values need a consistent tie-break so each subarray is counted exactly once.
connections.remove-k-digits: Turn monotonic removal into a greedy decision with a budget. A smaller incoming digit can improve the earliest differing position by removing a larger retained digit.
connections.asteroid-collision: Keep the cancellation idea but abandon the monotonic-value assumption. Only a right-moving survivor followed by a left-moving arrival can collide; magnitude alone is insufficient.
connections.car-fleet: Finish with a sorted simulation: process cars from nearest to farthest from the target and keep only arrival times that create new fleets. Sorting makes the no-overtaking constraint usable.
